title.narrative: Farming the bio way and milk collection farmers in the Eldoret region in Kenya

description.narrative: There is a growing demand in Kenya for high quality dairy products, such as yoghurt drinks, ice and pasteurized milk. Dutch company The Blue Link and its Kenyan subsidiary Bio Food Products ltd invested in a dairy factory in Nairobi which is now being upgraded to the latest industry standards through finance from DGGF and the Rabobank. The production of high quality dairy products, requires a constant intake of high quality raw milk. Technical Assistance through DGGF-TA was provided to secure this high quality milk in the supply chain, to minimise risks of the investment and to enhance sustainable impact for local farmers involved. The TA included 1) sustainable knowledge transfer regarding organic milk production, quality improvement and control, animal welfare and transport 2) the introduction of a controlled collection system, including protocols for quality control and cooled collection centres. The project was successful and resulted in 250 large and smallholder farmers benefiting from the training ‘Farming the Bio way’ which led to improved quality and increased production capacity of milk for these farmers. 100 of these farmers are now contracted by TBL to supply their milk and receive almost 30% higher prices for organic milk. Furthermore the project contributed to the professionalisation and sustainability of the entire dairy chain in the rural area of Eldoret, for example through the reduction of the use of antibiotics, improving animal welfare and feed and through bio certification of the farmers. A ‘train the trainer’ model and training guide was developed for future needs and additional farmers may be contracted to supply their milk in the near future.
